mechanism: An agency owner posts in a town Facebook group offering one free website to a local business. Many people comment, one is chosen, and the rejected commenters are offered a discount, which turns a single giveaway into several paying clients. It depends on the group's membership, the admin allowing the post, and the owner building a site quickly enough to make the giveaway credible. The numbers (3 clients per post, 5 to 6 runs) are self-reported by the speaker.
claim: A free-website giveaway post in a local Facebook group, followed by a discount for rejected commenters, brings about 3 clients per post over 5 to 6 runs.
why_not_testable: It needs a Facebook account, a real group and real people, and the only evidence is the speaker's own account.
needs: A Facebook account, membership of a local group with admin consent, and a site builder to deliver the free site.
one_line: A free-website giveaway in a town Facebook group turns the losing commenters into discounted clients, so one post is said to yield three.
idea_why: The give-first, proximity-based mechanism is plausible and cheap, but the conversion numbers are self-reported and untested outside the speaker's market.
breakdown: Pick a town group where local traders are active and read its rules on promotion. Post the offer, collect commenters over a few days, and choose one on a stated basis. Build the winner's site with Claude Code and a template, then message every other commenter with a time-limited discount. Track replies and closes in a simple sheet. A person would be needed to handle the Facebook posting and the conversations, since no script should do that for them.

missing: Nobody has a Facebook group presence or a record of how often this converts in a UK town.

mechanism: A vision-language model writes policy code and calls tools, while a vision-language-action or world-action model does the precise motor control. The harness decides what structure the VLM's code must have, which manipulation steps get tool or code help, and when the VLM is consulted at test time. The authors ran over 470,000 simulated rollouts across eight benchmarks, six VLMs and 15 VLA/WAM checkpoints to find which designs transfer. Their X-Harness recipe combines the findings without any weight updates.
claim: A harness recipe, X-Harness, lifts base robot policies by up to 42.8 points across memory, reasoning and domain-shift tasks without retraining.
why_not_testable: It needs robot simulators, GPUs and VLM/VLA checkpoints, none of which run keyless in 30 minutes.
needs: Robot simulation benchmarks, GPU time and model API access.
one_line: A robotics paper shows the scaffolding around a model moves success by tens of points with the same models, tested over 470,000 rollouts.
idea_why: Splitting slow reasoning from fast control and measuring the harness separately from the model is a well-supported design pattern.
breakdown: For Proteus the transferable piece is the method, not the robots. Treat any agent desk as model plus harness and vary the harness in controlled studies with the model fixed. That means writing the harness variants as config, running each over the same task set, and logging one success number per variant. Reading the paper's seven studies could suggest which harness variables matter most. No hired person is needed for the reading.

missing: Nobody has the simulators or compute to reproduce the robot results.

mechanism: It reconciles bank or payment statements against invoices using integer micro-unit arithmetic (BigInt) so no float rounding or model arithmetic is involved. Matching runs in layers: order ID, counterparty alias plus a date window, cross-currency spread, then a bounded subset-sum search for several charges against one consolidated invoice. The same server repairs mis-encoded CJK CSVs and writes spreadsheets that stop formula injection by storing cells as inline strings. It is exposed as MCP tools and billed per call through Apify.
claim: Three deterministic MCP tools reconcile statements to invoices for $0.02 a run with no external LLM call.
why_not_testable: It runs through npx from GitHub (Node install of an unvetted repo) and its main use is Chinese payment data Proteus does not have.
needs: Node 20 and real statement and invoice data to test against.
one_line: An MCP server does bank-to-invoice matching in integer arithmetic, including a bounded subset-sum pass for lumped invoices, so the model never does the sums.
idea_why: Keeping arithmetic and matching out of the model and in deterministic code is the right split for reconciliation.
breakdown: The same idea can be built in Python: parse statements into integer pence, match on reference first, then on amount and date window, then run a capped subset-sum for one-to-many cases. Output a report of matched, unmatched and ambiguous lines for a human to check. The data is the hard part: a bookkeeper or the client would supply sample statements. A hired person would review the ambiguous matches that no rule resolves.

mechanism: Audio is transcribed, then a model plays interviewer and asks about 15 follow-up questions to draw out detail, specifics and a point of view that the voice note lacked. The answers and the original transcript are then merged into one long-form first-person post. The result is posted to written platforms (Substack, Beehiiv, LinkedIn, X). The questioning pass is what separates it from plain transcript cleaning.
claim: Camera-shy operators can turn voice notes into long-form posts through a question-asking writer pass, then post to four written platforms.
why_not_testable: The question pass needs a model and there is no local LLM on this Mac, so it is not keyless tonight.
needs: A model for the interviewer and writer steps, and accounts on the target platforms.
one_line: A voice note goes in, a model asks about fifteen follow-up questions, and a first-person long-form post comes out for four written platforms.
idea_why: An interview pass that pulls in specifics fixes the usual thinness of transcript-to-article tools.
breakdown: Transcribe the voice note locally, then run a Claude Code skill that reads it and lists the gaps as questions. The person answers by voice again, and a second pass drafts the post in their own voice using a style guide. The draft is read and edited by the person before it goes anywhere. Posting to each platform stays manual or goes through a posting API. Someone must supply the real stories and opinions, since nothing in the pipeline can.
